## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over identity-ordered AoS with a list-based respawn intermediate can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Layout & approach
The 72 B/particle AoS layout wastes bandwidth: loop 1 touches 28 of 68 B/p (41% hot), loop 2 touches 4 of 68 B/p (5%), loop 3 touches 28 of 68 B/p (41%). The list intermediate adds 4 B/p for dead-index collection. With 59% dead bytes in integration/render loops, the line filler drags unused bytes through every 68B-stride iteration; the effective useful-bandwidth ceiling is ~12.3 GB/s (29.9 × 0.41). The working set spills L1d at N≈910 and L2 at N≈58254, turning the dead fraction into pure DRAM waste. The verdict stays in registers via in-loop `fcmp`/`b.lt` — branchy, not blended.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p is flat at 7.3–8.2 across all N from 380 to 10M — no knee at the L1d spill (N≈910) or L2 spill (N≈58254). The slight rise to 8.2 at N=10000 (L2-resident) is TLB pressure, not a cache event. This flatness means the algo is compute/overhead-bound at every regime, never reaching streaming speed. The dense grid confirms no transition changes cost.

## Bandwidth
At q=0.01, achieved 9.5–9.9 GB/s (32–33% of the 29.9 ceiling), 3.1x above the 2.408 ns/p floor — compute-bound. At q=0.5, achieved drops to 4.5–5.1 GB/s (15–17% of ceiling), 6.4x above floor — branch-bound, branch_flush at 35%. The algo is 1.0–1.02x baseline at q=0.01 (no gain over naive scalar), degrading to 1.11–1.20x at q=0.5. vs winner: 1.7–2.0x slower at q=0.01, worsening to 2.6–3.0x at q=0.5.

## Assembly
Loops 1/2 show partial component-wise vectorization: `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` with `ext.16b` to shuffle AoS components into contiguous lanes, plus `ld1.s {v17}[1]` single-element gather — vectorizing within one particle, not across particles. Loop 4 (render) is fully scalar: `fcmp`/`csel` chains (×18) for clamping, `fcvtzs` for float-to-int, `strb` byte-granular scatter (×16) for RGB writes that cannot coalesce. Only 18 of 352 instructions (5%) are vector-suffixed. The branchy death check (`fcmp`/`b.lt`) drives branch_flush rise with q.

## Verdict
Refuted — 1.0–1.02x of naive at q=0.01 and 1.7–2.0x slower than the winner across all N, sustaining only 32% of ceiling with no cache-spill knee. The partial component-wise vectorization (`fmul.4s` + `ext.16b`) cannot overcome the 41% hot-byte fraction or the scalar byte-scatter render loop. At q=0.5, branch_flush rises to 35% and the algo degrades to 1.11–1.20x of naive and 2.6–3.0x slower than the winner — the list-based respawn's branchy death check dominates.
